Vertical EAP With Load

In order to utilize the vertical set-up as a true actuator, the electrical energy from the volt source would have to somehow be transferred into mechanical energy beyond the simple expansion of the VHB itself. To this end, a load was glued to the VHB as previously described. Also, the permanent load as seen in the video is a 1.5 gram washer. In this configuration, the washer was raised 1.4 millimeters. When a 7.35 nut and bolt combination were integrated into the washer, the load was still lowered. The exact same distance was raised with this total 8.85 gram weight. Unfortunately, the rupturing of the VHB as seen above ended this load investigation before even more weight could be added. It is my inclination that much more weight could have been added without a decrease in distance traveled. This assertion comes simply from observing how the EAP did not seem to struggle or lose its structure at all under the 8.85 gram nut-washer-bolt combination. If energy for gravitational potential follows the form in Equation 8:
PEgravitational = mgh (Eqn. 8)
Where m is mass (kg), g is gravitational acceleration (~9.8 m/s²), and h is height (m), our larger load, while being lifted, would required: (.00885 Kg)*(9.8 m/s2)*(.0014 m) = 116.62 μJ.
Thus, electrical energy was converted to mechanical and the EAP did perform as an actuator. The true energy potential of this set-up would require more weight to be realized.
IX. Conclusions and the Road Ahead

As you can see, many aspects of high voltage Electrically Actuated Polymers have been explored. Personal highlights include the breakthrough achieved in Figure 4 and the successful application of load to the EAP as seen in the video link. Other significant findings include the calculation of the dielectric constant. Knowing that ε is a very normal value does however raise many questions. For instance, if ε is in fact slightly more than 1, how can the voltage on either side of the EAP stay insulated from each other? This is a valid question that deserves further investigation into the validity of the calculation of ε itself, as well as the physical and electrical properties of the VHB 4910 and the conductive carbon grease.

With more progress, more actuation properties can be quantified. Hopefully, the problem of how to integrate into the actual fin project can then be addressed. Even if electrical EAPs prove ineffective in water due to HV, their future significance cannot be overlooked. As one of the most promising breakthroughs in years in the fields of actuation, all projects in the LIMS lab could potentially benefit greatly from the future use of EAPs. Thus, the knowledge obtained through this project will surely pay-off down the road of innovation.
